Proceedings in the present case arises from filing of DAR by the investigating officer in FIR No.
446/22 PS Mundka SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.06.09 16:59:02 +0530 MACT No. 347/2024 Date of Award: 09.06.2025 regarding the accident in question.

As per the DAR, documents annexed therewith as well as material available on record, on 01.05.2022, while the petitioner was returning back to his home, at about 4:40 PM, when he reached in front of Metro Pillar No. 552, Main Rohtak Road, Mundka, Delhi, suddenly, a vehicle i.e.
bus bearing registration no. DL1PD5703 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle'), which was being driven by respondent no. 1 Hardeep in a fast speed and in rash and negligent manner, hit against the petitioner and his cart ('Rehri'), as a result of which, he fell down on the road and sustained injuries.

It is further stated that injured was taken to C.D. Global Hospital, Mundka,
Delhi, where he was medically examined vide MLC no. 141/22 dated 01.05.2022.

552, Mundka, Delhi bus stop to drop the passengers, suddenly one 'Rehri of Chhole Kulche' came from the wrong side overtaking near the bus stop and driver of the 'Rehri' was driving in rash and negligent manner and came from left side and hit the bus while overtaking the bus from the left side,
due to which, Ramesh, driver of the said 'Rehri' fell down from his 'Rehri' and received injuries; that no alleged accident has been caused from the vehicle due to rash and negligent driving of the driver Hardeep on the alleged date and place and he has been falsely implicated in the present case at the behest of the claimant in order to extort compensation amount from him.

In order to prove his case, petitioner examined himself as PW1, who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/1.
7.
No witness was got examined on behalf of the respondents.

8. I have heard arguments and gone through the record carefully and my issue wise findings are as under :
ISSUE No.1 9.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA

sentences.text: The onus to prove this issue was placed on the petitioner.
Petitioner/PW-1 Pradeep Kumar tendered his affidavit in evidence Ex.PW1/1 and relied upon the DAR filed by the police, which is Ex.P-1 (Colly).

In his cross-examination done by the Ld. counsel for the respondent no.3/insurance company, PW-1 stated inter alia that the accident took place between Mundka and Mundka Industrial Area; that he was coming from Mundka Industrial Area; that he was pushing his cart; that the bus hit him from behind; that the bus hit him first and then his cart; that he became unconscious after the accident; that somebody took him to the hospital; that he regained consciousness after 2-3 hours; that he was admitted to C.D. Global Hospital, Mundka, Delhi; that his cart got damaged and still lying in the police station; that he was discharged after 2-3 days; that thereafter, he went to his native village, where he took the desi treatment and bus driver was at fault in this accident.
He denied to the suggestion that he was deposing falsely and placing reliance on false documents.

In his cross examination done by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent no.1, he denied to the suggestion that he was crossing the road or that he came in front of the offending bus or that the accident took place due to his negligence.

He further stated that there was a red light at a distance of about 100-150 meters from the place of accident; that the driver of bus was talking on phone when the accident took place; that he cannot say that the driver stopped the bus at the bus stand for picking the passengers.
He denied to the suggestion that he overtook the bus or that he hit the stationary bus with his cart SACHIN

sentences.text: Petitioner / PW-1, who is injured in the present case, has well explained the mode and manner of the accident.
From the careful perusal of the testimony of the injured / PW-1 including his cross examination, there is nothing material has been elicited to disbelieve the version of accident as given by PW-1.
Rather evidence of PW-1 remained consistent on the aspect of accident, having been caused by rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 (driver of offending vehicle).

He has categorically deposed in his affidavit in evidence Ex.PW1/1 that the driver of the offending vehicle hit him and his 'Rehri', while driving the offending vehicle at a very fast speed and in rash and negligent manner and due to which, he suffered injuries.
Plea of the respondents that it was injured who was negligent due to which accident caused, has not been substantiated by any evidence.
Whereas, it is evident from the testimony of PW-1 that respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination.
Said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross-examination.
PW-1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against respondent no.1.
The testimony of PW-1 remained unimpeachable on the aspect of accident in question.
There is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner herein.

12. Further, the DAR filed by the IO includes the report u/s 173 Cr. PC filed by IO in FIR No. 446/22 PS Mundka; Site SACHIN by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.06.09 16:59:50 +0530 MACT No. 347/2024 Date of Award: 09.06.2025 plan of the place of accident; MLC, treatment record and medical/hospital bill of injured; Site plan; Mechanical inspection reports of the offending vehicle and 'Rehri' of injured; Seizure memo of offending vehicle and 'Rehri' of the injured; Documents of the offending vehicle; Arrest memo of accused (respondent no. 1 herein); Notice U/s 133 M.V. Act;
Statement of witnesses U/s 161 CrPC etc.

The respondent no. 1 namely Hardeep (accused in State case) has been charge-sheeted (which is part of copies of criminal case available on record) for offences punishable U/s 279/337 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.
Same also points out towards the rash and negligent driving of aforesaid vehicle by respondent no. 1 and corroborates the ocular testimony of PW1 to that extent.

The investigation was duly carried out which revealed not only the involvement of the offending vehicle, but also that it was the offending vehicle which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner which resulted in the accident.
There was an implicit duty on the respondent no.1 to see that his driving did not endanger the life of any other user of the road.
He has failed to exercise the caution incumbent upon him and has clearly neglected his duty of circumspection.

13. Moreover, apart from petitioner, the respondent no. 1 Hardeep was the other material witness who could have thrown sufficient light as to how and under what circumstances, the accident in question took place.
However, he did not enter into witness box during the course of inquiry.

Thus,
an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him for not entering into SACHIN by
SACHIN

GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.06.09 16:59:59 +0530 MACT No. 347/2024 Date of Award: 09.06.2025 the witness box, to the effect that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

sentences.text: Apart from above, copy of MLC report of injured shows that he was removed to C.D. Global Hospital on 01.05.2022 with alleged history of RTA.
On his examination, he was found to have sustained injuries as mentioned therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the said document from the side of respondents including insurance company.

15. Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that he had sustained injuries in road accident which took place on 01.05.2022 at about 4:40 PM at main Rohtak Road, in front of Metro Pillar no. 552, Mundka, Delhi due to the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
Accordingly, issue no.1 stands decided in favour of petitioner.
ISSUE No.2 16.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.06.09 17:00:07 +0530 MACT No. 347/2024 Date of Award: 09.06.2025
suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION Medical Expenses:
17. PW-1 i.e. the injured himself, has inter alia deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit that after the accident, he was taken to the C.D. Global Hospital, Mundka,
Delhi, wherein he remained admitted from 01.05.2022 to 03.05.2022; that since, he was not able to bear the hospital expenses, he took discharge from the hospital on 03.05.2022 and thereafter, he moved to his village and started taking desi treatment for his injuries.

In his cross-examination done by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent no.3, he stated that he was discharged after 2-3 days and thereafter, he went to his native village where he took the desi treatment.

He has relied upon DAR which is Ex.P-1.
18.

Ld. Counsel for petitioner has argued that petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.30,750/- during his hospitalization in the C.D. Global Hospital,
Mundka, Delhi from 01.05.2022 to 03.05.2022 and the medical bill is annexed by the IO alongwith the DAR.
19.

Petitioner has relied upon the DAR filed by IO which is Ex.P-1 which also consists of the MLC of petitioner and the medical bill No. 2022/1541 issued by C.D. Global Hospital, Mundka, Delhi in the name of patient/petitioner, amounting Rs.30,750/-.

sentences.text: There is nothing material elicited from the cross- examination of PW1, which would cast any doubt over the veracity and genuineness of the aforesaid medical bill and there is no reason to disbelieve the same.

In view of the aforesaid discussion as well as material available on record, the petitioner SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 17:00:17 +0530 Date: 2025.06.09 MACT No. 347/2024 Date of Award: 09.06.2025 is entitled to the above-mentioned bill amount i.e. Rs. 30,750/- under this head for medical expenses.
Loss of income during treatment period 20.

PW-1 has inter alia deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit that he was doing the work of selling 'chhole kulche' on his cart ('Rehri') and was earning Rs.500/- daily prior to the accident,
however, due to this accident, he was not able to do any work at all for more than one year and now,
he is earning Rs.200/- to Rs.250/- daily.

Counsel for petitioner has argued that due to the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the present accident, he remained bed ridden and could not do any work and therefore, he is entitled for an appropriate amount under this head.

Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the respondents have argued that as per the MLC of petitioner, he has suffered only simple injuries and there is no cogent evidence available on record to show that he was bed ridden for one year as alleged; that petitioner has failed to prove his alleged vocation as well as income and he is not entitled for any amount under this head.
22.
It is evident from record that at the time of accident, petitioner was also carrying his cart ('Rehri') with him.
He has deposed that he was earning Rs.500/- daily prior to the accident.

Thus,
his monthly income is taken as Rs. 15,000/ ( Rs. 500 X 30 days) for the purpose of computation of compensation in this case.
Further, As per the MLC of injured (which is part of Ex.P-1), he has suffered simple injuries in the accident.
Hospital bill filed by the IO alongwith the DAR shows that injured was hospitalized from 01.05.2022 to 03.05.2022.

However, there is no cogent evidence brought on record by the petitioner/injured in SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 17:00:25 +0530 Date: 2025.06.09 MACT No. 347/2024 Date of Award: 09.06.2025 support of his plea that he could not do any work for a period of one year due to this accident.

Hence, keeping in view of the nature of injuries, hospitalization of the injured/petitioner as well as surrounding circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that injured/petitioner would have not been able to work for a period of about one month.
Accordingly, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of sum of Rs.15,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 1 month) to the petitioner under this head towards loss of income.
Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
23. Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has argued that petitioner has suffered injuries due to this accident and and an appropriate amount should be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
Per contra, Ld. Counsel for respondents have argued that petitioner has not placed on record any document in support of his contentions for incurring expenses under this head.
Although, the petitioner has not filed any documentary evidence to prove expenses under this head, however, it cannot be overlooked that he had sustained simple injuries in the accident.

Thus, he would have Ramesh Kumar vs Hardeep And Ors on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118910375/
6 taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and would have also incurred some amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular checkup and follow up during the period of his medical treatment.

sentences.text: In the absence of any such documentary proof, this Tribunal while taking into consideration nature of injuries suffered by him as well as surrounding circumstances, finds it appropriate to grant a notional sum of Rs.10,000/- towards conveyance charges and special diet to the petitioner.

Keeping in view the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner as well as the facts and circumstances of the case, I hereby award a notional sum of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

25. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-
 S Heads of Compensation Amount  No.
 1. Medical expenses Rs. 30,750/-
 2 Loss of income during Rs. 15,000/-
 treatment period  3. Conveyance and Special diet Rs. 10,000/-
 4. Pain and Suffering Rs. 10,000/-

. Thus, the total compensation amount to which the petitioner is entitled comes to Rs. 65,750/-
(Rupees Sixty Five Thousand Seven Hundred and Fifty Only).
INTEREST ON AWARD 27.
Petitioner shall also be entitled to interest at the rate of 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the DAR i.e. 03.05.2024 till realization.
LIABILITY 28.
Now the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.

Since, it is an admitted case of the respondent No. 3 / Insurance Company that the aforesaid vehicle No. DL1PD5703 (offending vehicle) was duly insured with it, therefore, respondent No. 3 /
Insurance Co. is liable to pay the amount of compensation to the petitioner / claimant.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.

opennyai_summary.issue:
5. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed by this Tribunal on 26.07.2024:-
(i) Whether the petitioner Ramesh Kumar suffered injuries in a vehicular accident that took place on 01.05.2022 at about 4.40 pm at main Rohtak Road, in front of Metro Pillar no. 552, Mundka, Delhi involving a vehicle no. DL1PD5703 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no.1/Hardeep in a rash and negligent manner,
owned by respondent SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, at what amount and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Whereas, it is evident from the testimony of PW-1 that respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination.
The investigation was duly carried out which revealed not only the involvement of the offending vehicle, but also that it was the offending vehicle which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner which resulted in the accident.
There was an implicit duty on the respondent no.1 to see that his driving did not endanger the life of any other user of the road.
He has failed to exercise the caution incumbent upon him and has clearly neglected his duty of circumspection.
13. Moreover, apart from petitioner, the respondent no. 1 Hardeep was the other material witness who could have thrown sufficient light as to how and under what circumstances, the accident in question took place.
However, he did not enter into witness box during the course of inquiry.
Thus,
an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him for not entering into SACHIN by
Accordingly, issue no.1 stands decided in favour of petitioner.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.06.09 17:00:07 +0530 MACT No. 347/2024 Date of Award: 09.06.2025
Hence, keeping in view of the nature of injuries, hospitalization of the injured/petitioner as well as surrounding circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that injured/petitioner would have not been able to work for a period of about one month.
In the absence of any such documentary proof, this Tribunal while taking into consideration nature of injuries suffered by him as well as surrounding circumstances, finds it appropriate to grant a notional sum of Rs.10,000/- towards conveyance charges and special diet to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.facts:
From the careful perusal of the testimony of the injured / PW-1 including his cross examination, there is nothing material has been elicited to disbelieve the version of accident as given by PW-1.
Rather evidence of PW-1 remained consistent on the aspect of accident, having been caused by rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 (driver of offending vehicle).
